CVE-2026-112375.title: Apache Kafka: Unauthorized principal can read arbitrary broker files via IncrementalAlterConfigs
CVE-2026-112375.description:
An authenticated Kafka principal with no authorization grants (not even ALTER_CONFIGS) can make a broker read a file or an environment variable from the broker host and return its contents. An IncrementalAlterConfigs (or AlterConfigs) request targeting a BROKER resource reaches the broker's configuration validation before any authorization check is applied to that path. Validation resolves configuration variables such as ${file:/path:key} or ${env:VAR} using a ConfigProvider named in the request, and this resolution bypasses the org.apache.kafka.automatic.config.providers allowlist that was added as the mitigation for CVE-2024-31141. An arbitrary ConfigProvider (for example FileConfigProvider or EnvVarConfigProvider) is therefore instantiated and the referenced file or environment variable is read, and a type-validation error returns the resolved content to the caller.

CVE-2026-99465.title: media: microchip-isc: take a reference on the parsed endpoints
CVE-2026-99465.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: microchip-isc: take a reference on the parsed endpoints

for_each_endpoint_of_node() drops the reference on the current node as
it advances. xisc_parse_dt() and isc_parse_dt() store the node in
subdev_entity->epn and release it later with of_node_put(), but never
took their own reference, so the stored pointer refers to an
already-released node. This underflows the refcount and can
use-after-free, reachable through the camera device tree overlay.

Take a reference with of_node_get() when storing the node, and drop it
in microchip_isc_subdev_cleanup() so the entities the bind loop never
reaches on an early exit do not leak it.

control chunks pointing at the old socket. A later retransmission can
therefore access the socket after it has been freed.

Extend the migration walk to cover retained control chunks and use
sctp_control_set_owner_w() to assign their new owner. Reuse the DATA
ownership check so each chunk is processed once per pass, even when it
is reachable through multiple lists or retained pointers.

Preserve a control chunk's existing authentication key across migration
so its final release can still generate SCTP_AUTH_FREE_KEY when needed.

CVE-2026-99601.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: check the unallocated space table when it is loaded

udf_table_new_block() hands out the first block of the extent closest
to its goal and trusts that the extent covers at least one whole block
inside the partition. Nothing checks that. A zero-length extent makes
it return the block the extent points at, which need not be free, and
the subtraction of one block then underflows the length into the type
bits, turning the entry into a bogus continuation. An extent running
past the end of the partition makes it return blocks behind the
partition.

Such tables are not only found on crafted images: until the previous
commit, udf_table_new_block() itself left zero-length extents behind
in tables written by mkudffs, and then converted them into extents
running past the partition.
